answer: Memory-hard proof-of-work resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to solve an epoch-bound puzzle that fills large memory arrays before peers admit its messages. Agents coordinating tasks like inspecting a steel bridge, mapping a sloped terrace, or tracking a willow stand must prove dedicated RAM bandwidth and electricity per identity, though verification stays cheap. While this raises marginal hardware and power costs, adversaries renting bulk cloud memory can still outscale smaller nodes.
